questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door on the passenger side
Above the emergency door in the rear
Under the driver's seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. It lets the driver watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: What should you do when encountering a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle if it is going too slowly on the tracks.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is a task you may be asked to do during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.
Drive in a figure eight.
Alley dock.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: Tasks in the basic vehicle control skills test include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What should a school bus driver do when students are boarding?

options.text: Read a book.
Check all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all mirrors.
questions.explanation: While students board, the driver should supervise and watch all mirrors for students running to catch the bus.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the proper railroad crossing procedures at a simulated location.

questions.question: What should a driver do if a bus stalls on railroad tracks?

options.text: Evacuate the bus and move everyone far away from the tracks.
Keep everyone in the bus and try to wave the train down.
Keep everyone in the bus and wait for help.
Keep everyone in the bus and call a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Evacuate the bus and move everyone far away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, evacuate everyone immediately. Lead students away from the bus at an angle in the direction of any oncoming train to avoid debris.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, school bus mirrors allow the driver to see ____ behind the bus.

options.text: 50 feet
100 feet
200 feet
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is critical for safe school bus operation. Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet, or four bus lengths, behind the bus.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror should be mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which task will you NOT be required to do?

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You will not need to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, school bus mirrors allow the driver to see ____ behind the bus.

options.text: One bus length
Two bus lengths
Three bus lengths
Four bus lengths

questions.correctAnswerText: Four bus lengths
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is critical for safe school bus operation. Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet, or four bus lengths, behind the bus.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are hard to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits make noise.
The emergency exits cannot be opened from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits must open smoothly, be in good condition, and close securely from the inside.

questions.question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following except:

options.text: Look for missing leaf springs.
Look for broken coil springs.
Make sure torsion springs are not damaged.
Glue cracked leaf springs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glue cracked leaf springs.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Check for broken or bent coil springs. If the vehicle has torsion bars, torque arms, or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are mounted firmly.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills.
Listen to the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.
Drive in an unsafe way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must listen to and follow the examiner's directions. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: A passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Has a control device.
Does not have any control devices.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not have any control devices.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: ABS allows a driver to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps prevent the wheels from locking up. This helps the driver stay in control when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, adjust the mirrors:

options.text: While driving.
Before you start to drive.
After the drive is finished.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start to drive.
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is critical for safe school bus operation. Always check all mirrors before you start driving the bus.

questions.question: When students are being picked up by a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students who are walking to a designated bus stop.
Parents may choose where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers can only pick up students at official bus stops set by school officials.

questions.question: Which of the following causes the most student deaths per year?

options.text: Students getting on and off school buses
Accidents involving drunk drivers
Accidents caused by careless driving
Accidents in which drivers ignore traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students getting on and off school buses
questions.explanation: More students are killed each year while getting on or off school buses than while riding inside them.

questions.question: To safely unload a bus, students should:

options.text: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
Stand up and move toward the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit the bus and stand right next to it while it is driving away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
questions.explanation: Students should stay seated until the driver says it is safe to exit. After getting off, they should move at least 10 feet away from the bus so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your on-road driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross the tracks at a pretend location.
